_comment: What each planted violation does to `make -C proxy lint`, machine-readable,
for the reason ci/broken-inputs/*/expect.json gives everywhere else: prose in
GATE.md is not a declaration, and a count or a case stated only in prose
drifts the moment a tool is configured differently.
`tool` is the mix task the input exists to provoke, and it is matched against
the lint recipe in ci/make/elixir.mk rather than against a list here -- a tool
added to lint with no input naming it fails.
`fails` is the EXACT set of lint commands expected to fail on this tree. Five
of the six are singletons, which is the property this whole directory exists
to demonstrate: the tool refuses, and the other five stay blind. `tool` has to
be IN `fails`: without that the pairing is a label, and swapping two trees'
`tool` fields changed nothing measured while unbinding both tools from the
inputs that name them.
`case` is a substring the failing tool's own output has to carry, so a tool
exiting non-zero for an unrelated reason is not read as a demonstration. It is
required, because a tree with no `case` accepts any non-zero exit at all, and
it has to be absent from what the same tool says about a CLEAN copy -- a case
the tool prints either way separates nothing from nothing.
`plants` is the exact set of files the tree lays over proxy/, checked in both
directions -- a declared file that is absent planted nothing, and a file in
the tree that is undeclared changes the copy in a way nothing asserts about.
`why_not_alone` is required per tool in `fails` other than `tool`, and is a
`because` plus a `forced_by` citation -- a file and a string in it that the
check looks up. A sentence alone would license an arbitrarily large declared
failing set for the price of writing one.
`derived_from` marks a fixture file that EXTENDS a real one and must still
contain it, so drift in the real file is named rather than inferred.

dialyzer.because: `mix dialyzer` builds the project before it analyses it, and mix.exs sets warnings_as_errors in every environment, so a compile-warning plant fails Dialyzer before analysis starts. Half of that is decidable here and is the half `forced_by` cites; the other half is dialyxir's own build-then-analyse behaviour, which was measured rather than read. Measured too: the other four tools stay silent on this tree. Recorded rather than engineered around -- the alternative is a warning Dialyzer does not trigger on, which would be a fixture shaped by the check instead of by the tool.

tree-credo.case: Functions should have a @spec type specification.

tree-dialyzer.case: The @spec for the function does not match the success typing
